svg.title: URL SHORTENER (BITLY): sketchnote
svg.text: It sounds like a toy, but it is the cleanest example of a read-heavy system:
almost every request is a redirect.
Redirects outnumber new links about 100 to 1, so
the design is mostly about serving reads fast.
Generate short codes from a counter encoded in
base62: unique by construction, no collision
Put a cache in front of the database; a small
share of links gets most clicks, so the hit rate is
Create a short URL for a long URL (optional
Start simple: a write service creates a code and
stores it in Postgres. ~12 writes/sec is
reads/sec straight to Postgres is what breaks
straight to Postgres is what breaks first.
Add a Redis cache (code → URL). Clicks follow
Pareto, so 80%+ hit the cache in under 1ms.
Postgres only sees misses; add replicas if needed.
Generate codes from a global counter: Redis INCR
+ base62. 7 chars = 3.5 trillion codes, no collisions.
Servers grab IDs in batches of 1,000.
How do you guarantee unique codes?
Counter + base62 is unique by construction. Hashing (MD5 prefix) needs a unique constraint
